label: Render Image…
params: {path?, width?, height?, camera?, grid?}; writes a PNG, or without a path returns it as {png: base64} (at most 2048 on a side). camera: an object with a camera component; default: the first camera in the scene, else a view framing every object

label: List Objects
params: none; returns the object tree

label: Show Scene Document
params: none; returns {path, dirty, scene}: every object and component, as the scene file holds them

label: List Component Types
params: none

label: Create Object
params: {parent?, name?, index?, components?: {name: value or null}}; returns {id}

label: Delete Object
params: {id}

label: Duplicate
params: {id}; the copy, with its children, goes right after the original. Returns {id}

label: Copy
params: {ids: [id, ...]}; returns the objects and their children as clipboard data for scene.object.paste

label: Paste
params: {objects: <data from scene.object.copy>, parent?: id, index?: n}; returns the new {ids}

label: Move Up
params: {id}; moves before the previous sibling

label: Move Down
params: {id}; moves after the next sibling

label: Make Child of Previous
params: {id}; becomes the last child of the previous sibling

label: Move Out of Parent
params: {id}; moves right after its parent

label: Add Script
params: {id, module}; module: .wasm or .bscript path relative to the project folder (or the scene file's folder outside a project); returns {index}

label: Remove Script
params: {id, index}

label: Set Script Property
params: {id, index, name, value}: value is a number, true/false, three numbers or text, as the script declares the property (an object property: the object's name); null returns to the script's default

label: Inspect Object
params: {id}; returns {id, parent, children, components}

label: Move Object
params: {id, parent?, index?, keepWorld? = true}; parent null moves to the root

label: Set Component Value
params: {id, component, value}

label: Add Component
params: {id, component}

label: Remove Component
params: {id, component}

label: Reset Component
params: {id, component, script?}: puts every field back to its default; with script (an index, component "scripts") only that script's properties, to their declared defaults. On a prefab copy the prefab file's values are used instead, where the file has them. Returns {from: "defaults"} or {from: "prefab", source}

label: Play
params: {scripts?: "interpreted" | "compiled"} (default interpreted); returns {scripts, running, runtime}

label: Stop
params: none; restores the scene as it was before play
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Pause or Resume
params: none; toggles pause
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Step
params: {seconds? = 1/60, steps? = 1}; advances play mode, also when paused
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Set Held Keys
params: {keys: [names], pointer?: [x, y] (-1 to 1, +y up; null when outside the view), buttons?: n (bit 0 left, 1 right, 2 middle), pad?: {axes: [left x, left y, right x, right y, left trigger, right trigger], buttons: [South, East, …]}}; what scripts see as held, until the next call or the next editor frame
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Read Console
params: {last?: n (default 100), errors?: true for errors only}; returns {lines: [{level, text}], total}: the newest lines, oldest first

label: Clear Console
params: none

label: Game State
params: none; the game's values and each player's (both empty at first), saved values kept between plays (in the project's saves/progress.json), and outcome: "won", "lost" or null

label: Set Game Value
params: {name, value, player?, saved?}: sets a value in the game's state, a player's (an object with Player Control) or, with saved: true, a saved one; play mode only
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Clear Saved Values
params: none; forgets the values the game saved in the project, and in play mode the ones it holds

label: Cast Physics Ray
params: {origin: [x, y, z], direction: [x, y, z], distance? = 1000}; the first collider or character hit (triggers left out), in play mode or in the scene as it is: {hit, object?, name?, distance?, point?, normal?}

label: Load Scene in Play
params: {path, additive?}: a .bscene relative to the project; added to the playing scene, or in its place (scripts restart, the game state stays); returns {objects}
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Unload Scene in Play
params: {path}: removes the scenes added from that file while playing; returns {removed}
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Scenes Added in Play
params: none; returns {added: [{path, objects}]}
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Play Status
params: none; returns {playing, paused, time, scripts, running, console}

label: Send Message
params: {name, value?, id?}: sends the scripts of object id (or of every object) the message now, as a script's send does
disabledReason: messages go to scripts while the game plays

label: Sounds Playing
params: none; returns {heard, sounds: [{id, source, object, seconds, looping, volume}]}: the sounds playing now (heard is false where play is silent)
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Play Sound
params: {id}: plays the object's Audio Source; returns {sound}
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Stop Sound
params: {id}: stops the sounds the object plays; returns {stopped}
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Streamed Areas
params: none; returns {areas: [{id, name, scene, loadDistance, keepMargin, state, objects, problem?}]}: every Streamed Area in the playing scene; state is away, waiting, reading, here or failed
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Wait for Streamed Areas
params: {seconds?}: waits (at most seconds, default 10, up to 60) until no Streamed Area is being read, and adds those that arrived; returns {here, busy}
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Split into Streamed Areas…
params: {cellSize, folder, loadDistance?, keepMargin?}: moves the open scene's top objects into one .bscene per grid cell (cellSize wide, by X and Z) in folder (relative to the project; the files must not be there yet), and puts a Streamed Area for each cell under a new Streamed World object. Cameras, sun lights, environment, game rules, player starts and players stay. loadDistance defaults to 1.5 cells, keepMargin to a quarter cell; returns {world, areas: [{id, scene, objects}], moved}

label: Export Game…
params: {folder, platform?, mode?, player?}: writes the open project as a game into a new folder named after it inside folder: the player program under the game's name, and its scenes, assets and scripts in one file, game.pack, beside it (visual scripts compiled; Rust sources, build output and saved values left out; in native mode the pack is built into the program). platform is windows, linux, mac or web (default: this computer's); mode is how scripts run: interpreted, compiled or native (default: the project's choice for the platform); player is the program built on another system, or for the web the folder of the web player (default: the one cargo xtask web-player built). For the web the folder holds index.html, the web player and game.pack (the game's files in one file) instead. Refused, with the reasons, when project.export.check finds an error; returns {path, program, files, compiled, skipped}
disabledReason: open a project first

label: Check Export
params: {platform?, mode?, player?}: whether the open project can be exported for platform with its scripts run in mode (defaults as for project.export), without writing anything; returns {platform, mode, ready, findings: [{severity: error|warning|note, message, file?}], scripts: [{path, kind, runs, note}], files}
disabledReason: open a project first

label: Scene Settings
params: none; returns the open scene's own settings: {lighting}

label: Change Scene Settings
params: {lighting?, postProcessing?}: the lighting asset (.blight, relative to the project folder; empty for the engine's light) and the post-processing asset (.bpost; empty for none) the scene uses; returns the settings

label: Read Lighting
params: {path}: a lighting asset (.blight); returns {lighting: {skyColor, horizonColor, groundColor, ambient, showSky, fogDistance, sun: {enabled, rotation, color, intensity, shadows}}}

label: Change Lighting
params: {path, lighting}: writes a lighting asset (the whole lighting, as lighting.get returns it); every scene that names it changes

label: Read Post-processing
params: {path}: a post-processing asset (.bpost); returns {post: {toneMapping, bloom, color (with lookup, lookupStrength), vignette, depthFog, occlusion, antialiasing}}

label: Change Post-processing
params: {path, post}: writes a post-processing asset (all of it, as post.get returns it); every scene and camera that names it changes. A colour lookup image (color.lookup) of the wrong size is refused; one not there yet is a warning

label: Make Neutral Lookup
params: {path, steps?}: writes a colour lookup image (.png) that changes no colour, steps (2 to 64, default 16) squares of steps by steps side by side, to recolour in an image editor and name in color.lookup; returns {path, relative} (relative to the project). Refuses a file that is already there

label: Read Data Shape
params: {path}: a data shape (.bshape, relative to the project folder or absolute); returns {shape: {fields: [{name, type, default, label?, hint?, range?, slider?, group?}]}}. type is as scripts declare property types: number, whole, bool, vector, color, text, object, prefab, sound, material, data, or list:<type>, map:<type> (text keys), map:<key type>:<type>

label: Change Data Shape
params: {path, shape}: writes a data shape (all of it, as data.shape.get returns it); every data file that names it reads its fields from then on: a value that no longer fits reads as the field's default and is reported by data.get

label: Read Data File
params: {path}: a data file (.bdata); returns {data: {shape, values}, fields: [{name, type, value, set}] (every field of its shape as it reads, set when the file gives the value), problems: [text]}

label: Change Data File
params: {path, data: {shape, values}}: writes a data file (all of it): the shape it names (.bshape, relative to the project folder; empty for none) and the values that differ from the shape's defaults, by field name

label: Change Data Field
params: {path, name, value}: sets one field of a data file to a value that fits the field in its shape (as data.get shows values); value null returns it to the shape's default. Refuses names the shape lacks

label: Record Profile
params: none: records each play step's time by part, and what the views draw, until profile.stop

label: Stop Profile
params: none: stops recording; the frames recorded stay

label: Clear Profile
params: none: forgets the frames recorded

label: Profile Frames
params: {last?}: the last frames recorded (all, at most 3000): {recording, gpuMeasured, frames: [{time, step, scripts, byScript, physics, streaming, sound, particles, extract, draw, gpu, drawCalls, triangles, meshBytes, imageBytes}], average}; gpu is the GPU's own time (null where the device gives no timestamps: gpuMeasured false; null while unknown)

label: Graph Node Kinds
params: {domain: "material" | "script" | "animation"}

label: New Graph
params: {domain: "material" | "script" | "animation"}

label: Open Graph
params: {path} (.bmaterial or .bscript)

label: Save Graph
params: {path?} (needed for a graph that has no file yet)
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Close Graph
params: {id?}: closes the graph in use (or the open graph id) with its undo steps; the one opened before it is then in use

label: Show Graph
params: none; returns the graph in use: {id, domain, path, dirty, graph, problems, outputTypes}; outputTypes says what each number-or-vector output gives now, by its inputs: [{node, pin, type}]

label: Open Graphs
params: none; the open graphs, each in a tab of its own: {graphs: [{id, domain, path, dirty, inUse}]}

label: Use Graph
params: {id} or {path}: makes that open graph the one the graph.* commands work on

label: Add Node
params: {kind, position: [x, y]}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Remove Node
params: {node}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Move Node
params: {node, position: [x, y]}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Set Node Value
params: {node, name, value} (null restores the default)
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Copy Nodes
params: {nodes: [id]}: returns {text}, the nodes and the links between them as clipboard text
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Paste Nodes
params: {text, offset?: [x, y]}: adds copies of copied nodes with new ids; returns {nodes, skipped}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Duplicate Nodes
params: {nodes: [id]}: adds copies beside them, linked as the originals are to each other; returns {nodes, skipped}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Link Pins
params: {from: {node, pin}, to: {node, pin}}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Unlink Pin
params: {node, pin}: removes every link at that pin
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Add Comment
params: {position: [x, y], size?: [w, h], text?}: a box behind nodes, with a note; returns {comment}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Edit Comment
params: {comment, text?, position?, size?}
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Remove Comment
params: {comment}: the nodes in it stay
disabledReason: open or create a graph first

label: Add Variable
params: {name, type: "number" | "wholeNumber" | "vector" | "trueFalse" | "text" | "object" | "color", shape?, key?, start?}: declares a variable of a visual script, starting at start (else zero); shape "list" or "map" makes it a list (items in order, by index from 0) or a map (values under keys of type key, else text) of that type, starting empty or with start ([...] or {...})

label: Change Variable
params: {name, rename?, type?, shape?, key?, start?}: a new start value, a new name that the variable's nodes follow, or a new type, shape ("single", "list", "map") or map key type (key); the start stays where it still fits, else it goes to zero, and its nodes follow the new type

label: Remove Variable
params: {name}: its nodes keep working, starting from zero

label: Add Property
params: {name, type, shape?, key?, default?}: declares a property of a visual script (type and shape as for variables), with a default (else zero); the Inspector sets it per object

label: Change Property
params: {name, rename?, type?, shape?, key?, default?, inspector?}: a new default, a new type or shape (as for variables; options that no longer fit go), a new name that its Property and Set Property nodes follow, or how the Inspector shows it ({label?, hint?, group?, range?, slider?, readOnly?, choices?, showIf?}; {} for a plain row)

label: Remove Property
params: {name}: its nodes stay, reading zero where no object sets it

label: Add Function
params: {name}: declares a function of a visual script, with no inputs or outputs yet; its Function node begins its actions, Return gives back its outputs and Call Function runs it

label: Change Function
params: {name, rename?, inputs?, outputs?}: a new name, or new inputs or outputs ([{name, type}], type as for variables); the function's nodes follow, and links to pins that went away go

label: Remove Function
params: {name}: its nodes stay, and say they name no function

label: Add Event
params: {name}: declares an event of a visual script, bringing no values yet; its On Event nodes run when a script or the interface triggers it on the object, and Trigger Event nodes trigger it

label: Change Event
params: {name, rename?, params?}: a new name, or new values ([{name, type}], type as for variables); the event's nodes follow, and links to pins that went away go

label: Remove Event
params: {name}: its nodes stay (a Trigger Event may name another script's event)

label: Set Menu Path
params: {path}: where Add Component lists the visual script (Light/Flicker); empty for under Scripts

label: New Project…
params: {path, name?}: makes the folder `path` (it must not exist or be empty) with a starting scene, a material and a visual script, then opens the scene

label: Open Project…
params: {path}: a .bproject file or its folder; opens the project's main scene

label: Project Info
params: none; the open project's folder, name and main scene, or null

label: Project Settings
params: none; returns {project, settings}: the open project's settings (physics: {enabled, gravity, precision: "single" | "double"}, input: {map: the project's Input Map, a .binput file (see input.asset)}), or the defaults and project: false outside a project

label: Change Project Settings
params: {settings}: the whole settings object, written to the project file; play mode uses it from its next start
disabledReason: open a project first; scenes outside a project use the default settings

label: Save as Prefab
params: {id, path}: saves the object and its children to a .bprefab file and links the object to it

label: Place Prefab
params: {path, parent?, index?}: adds a linked copy of a .bprefab file; returns {id}

label: Apply to Prefab
params: {id}: writes this copy to its prefab file and updates the other copies in the scene; returns {updated}

label: Revert to Prefab
params: {id}: replaces this copy's objects with the prefab file's, keeping its name and transform

label: Open Prefab
params: {path}: edits the prefab on its own: the scene and its undo history wait underneath, and prefab.close goes back; returns {source, depth}

label: Save Prefab
params: none: writes the open prefab to its file; returns {path}
disabledReason: no prefab is open

label: Back from Prefab
params: {discard?}: goes back to the scene (or the prefab) underneath, whose copies update from the file; refuses unsaved changes unless discard
disabledReason: no prefab is open

label: New Script
params: {folder, name}: makes a Rust script crate `folder/<name>/` from a template; returns {path, module}

label: Build Script
params: {path}: a script crate folder; builds it to WebAssembly next to the folder; returns {module, log}

label: File Info
params: {path}: a file or folder, relative to the project folder or absolute; returns {path, kind, bytes, rows: [[label, value]], problems, text?}

label: Create Asset
params: {kind: "folder" | "scene" | "material" | "visualScript" | "script" | "inputMap" | "lighting" | "postProcessing" | "interface" | "interfaceStyle" | "dataShape" | "dataFile", folder, name}: makes it in the folder (relative to the project folder or absolute); returns {path}, and for a script {path, module}

label: List Assets
params: {path?, recursive?}: what a folder of the project holds (the project folder when left out), as the Project panel lists it: hidden and build folders left out. Returns {entries: [{path, kind}], truncated}, paths relative to the project folder

label: Delete Asset
params: {path, permanent?}: moves a file or folder of the project (relative to the project folder or absolute) to the Recycle Bin; permanent: true deletes it for good, for where there is no Recycle Bin. Never the project folder itself. A Rust script leaves the project's workspace with it

label: Rename Asset
params: {path, name}: renames a file or folder of the project (relative to the project folder or absolute); a file keeps its extension when the name leaves it out; a Rust script's folder renames its crate, its built module and its workspace entry too. Never over another file. Returns {path}

label: Import Files
params: {files: [path], folder?}: copies models (.glb, .gltf with the files it names), images (.png, .jpg) and sounds into a folder of the project (relative to the project folder; the project folder when left out), each read first, so a file that cannot be read says why and nothing is copied. A name already taken gets a number. Models and images get import settings beside them. A file already in the project stays where it is. Returns {imported: [{path, kind, source}]}, paths relative to the project folder

label: Import Settings
params: {path}: how a model or image of the project is read: {settings: {model?: {scale, upAxis: "y" | "z"}, image?: {mipmaps}}, saved}; saved is false while it has only the defaults

label: Set Import Settings
params: {path, settings: {model?: {scale, upAxis}, image?: {mipmaps}}}: saves how a model or image is read, beside it; scenes using it read it again. Returns {path} of the settings file

label: Place File
params: {path, parent?, index?, position?: [x, y, z]}: a model or a sound of the project as a new object named after it (a Mesh drawing the model, or an Audio Source playing the sound), at position (world units; the origin when left out). Returns {id}

label: Apply Image
params: {id, image}: an image of the project becomes the object's look: a sprite shows it; a mesh gets a new material beside the image that shows it (named after it). Returns {material?}: the material made

label: Read Interface
params: {path}: an interface layout (.bui) as {layout: {format, version, styles, root}}

label: Write Interface
params: {path, layout}: checks and writes an interface layout (.bui): elements {kind, name?, classes?, text?, image?, value?, min?, max?, bind?, style?, children?}

label: Add Interface Element
params: {path, into?, kind, index?}: adds an element of kind to a layout, inside the element at into (child indices from the root; the root when left out), at index or last. Returns {at}

label: Remove Interface Element
params: {path, at}: removes the element at at (child indices from the root) and what it holds

label: Move Interface Element
params: {path, at, into, index}: moves the element at at into the element at into, at index (counted without it). Returns {at}

label: Edit Interface Element
params: {path, at, element: {kind?, name?, classes?, text?, image?, layout?, onClick?, value?, min?, max?, bind?, style?}}: changes the given fields of the element at at; style replaces the element's whole style

label: Save Interface Part
params: {path, at, to}: writes the element at at, with what it holds, as a layout file of its own (to, a new .bui) and puts a part using it in its place; inside it, its names are then <part>/<name>

label: Read Interface Style
params: {path}: an interface style file (.bstyle) as {style: {format, version, rules}}

label: Write Interface Style
params: {path, style}: checks and writes a style file (.bstyle): rules {kind | class | name, set: {property: value}}

label: Interface State
params: {id}: while playing, the object's interface as it shows: {visible, elements: [{name, kind, text, value, visible}]} for its named elements

label: Press Interface Element
params: {id, element}: while playing, presses a button or an element with On Click (its scripts get pressed:<name>, and the On Click message) or flips a toggle (changed:<name>), as the player would

label: Change Interface Element
params: {id, element, value? | text?}: while playing, sets a slider's or toggle's value or a text field's text as the player would; its scripts get changed:<name>

label: Read Input Map
params: {path}: a .binput file; returns {asset: {start, maps: [{name, actions: [{name, kind: "trigger" | "held" | "value", bindings: [key:W | mouse:Left | pad:South | axis:LeftX+]}]}]}, maps, problem}; scripts name an action map/action

label: Change Input Map
params: {path, asset: {start, maps: [{name, actions: [{name, kind, bindings}]}]}}: checks the maps and actions (names of letters, digits and _, unique; known bindings) and writes the file; play mode reads it from its next start

label: Set Input Map
params: {map, object?}: makes a map active, in the project's Input Map or an object's own (Input Map component); play mode only
disabledReason: play mode is not running

label: Input State
params: none; in play mode the active map of the project's Input Map and of each object's own, with their maps

label: New Keyframe Animation
params: {prefab, length?, path?}: opens a new timeline for the .bprefab file (length in seconds, 2 if left out); with path it is written there at once

label: Open Keyframe Animation
params: {path} (.btimeline)

label: Save Keyframe Animation
params: {path?} (needed for a timeline that has no file yet)

label: Close Keyframe Animation

disabledReason: open or create a timeline first (timeline.open, timeline.new)

label: Add Track

label: Record Key

label: Record Keys

label: Play Keyframe Animation

label: Stop Keyframe Animation

label: Read Animation
params: {id}: the object's animation: {clips: [{name, duration}], joints: [names], layers: [{joint, motion, time, fading}], parameters: {name: value}, playing, state (the animation state it is in, or null), states (its states' names, or null)}

params: {id, name}: sets a trigger, which the first transition that uses it uses up

label: Preview Clip
params: {id, clip, time?: seconds, playing?: true/false}: outside play mode, shows the clip on the object's model in the views (the Inspector's preview), looping: from `time` when given (scrubbing), moving while `playing`; the scene file does not change

label: Stop Preview
params: {id}: ends the object's preview; the views show its Model Animation again

label: Read Joint
params: {id, joint}: where the joint of the object's model is in the world now, as its animation poses it (at rest when nothing plays): {position, rotation (degrees), scale}

label: Go to Animation State
params: {id, state, fade?: seconds}: an object running animation states goes to that state now, fading over `fade` (default 0.25)
